newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: rugby union-Australian Wallabies beat Connacht 37-20.
newsitem.headline: rugby union-Australian Wallabies beat Connacht 37-20.

text.p: Australia's rugby union touring side produced a second-half try-burst to foil courageous Connacht's victory bid on Wednesday, ending up 37-20 winners after trailing 7-12 at the interval.
The Irish provincial side scented a famous win when outside half Eric Elwood's fifth penalty early in the second half increased the lead to eight points.
But Australia stepped up a gear to grab four tries and run out comfortable winners in their first game of the Irish leg of their tour.
Wing David Campese had a quiet afternoon attempting to regain his test place back for the match against Ireland on Saturday week to add to his 100 caps.
But Campese was mobbed at the final whistle by a crowd of youngsters in what is probably his last appearance at Galway's sports ground on the west coast of Ireland.
Scrum half George Cregan sparked Australia's comeback when he was rewarded for supporting a break by number eight Owen Finegan with a try.
Cregan scored again when he darted over from close range after Finegan had been held up as Australia increased the pressure on the Connacht forwards.
Finegan got in on the tryscoring act himself to make the game safe for the tourists.
But it was the Irish who had the crowd -- and themselves -- in hysterics when they scored a late consolation try.
The Australians were flummoxed when the whole Connacht team, apart from the thrower and the scrum-half , formed a line-out close to the visitors' line.
Lock Graham Heaslip won the ball and as the whole team drove on it was fellow second row Shane Leahy, who played for Ireland A against South Africa on Tuesday, who was credited with the try.
The Irish were still laughing as Australia's centre Alistair Murdoch ghosted through the defence to bring up the fifth try in the final seconds.
It had all looked so different in the first half which was dominated by the boot of Elwood who had also played against South Africa.
Elwood kicked his side into the five-point advantage at the break with four well-taken penalties.
The Australians response was a try by lock Tim Gavin as he took advantage of a three-man overlap.
Full-back Tim Wallace kicked the conversion and added three more as well as two penalties to give Australia an easy victory in the end.

Campese said: "All credit to Connacht, they played extremely well in the first half to lead. Our coach told us just to keep our discipline. But every time we went forward in the second half I felt we were going to score a try."
Campese knows it is going to be difficult to force his way back into the test line-up after being dropped for the game against Scotland last week.
"Selection is going to be very hard," said the 34-year-old, who is determined to win back his international place before the tour ends.
"I need to get involved in games, especially if I'm not scoring, so that I can contribute in some way.
"But we'll just have to wait and see what team is picked for the Ulster match on Saturday. I know nothing about them.
"There are 30 good guys out here wanting to be in the team. I may get more recognition than them, but that's because I've been around a lot longer."
